full_form: Classic Hodgkin Lymphoma -> Hodgkin lymphoma, NOS (9650)
notes: Abbreviation for classic Hodgkin lymphoma, distinguishing it from NLPHL (9659). Codes 9650 unsubtyped. EBER positivity in classic HL overall is about 40%, mixed cellularity 70-80% and HIV-related classic HL over 90% — a positive EBER here is expected and weakly informative.

full_form: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma -> Hodgkin lymphoma, NOS (9650)

full_form: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma -> Hodgkin lymphoma, NOS (9650)

Older abbreviation for Hodgkin's disease, still written by clinicians trained before WHO 2001. Maps to 9650. confidence=medium because 'HD' is also written for Hodgkin's disease and for unrelated non-oncological terms — confirm against the report text.

Standard abbreviation and a high-frequency search term. Maps to the lineage-unresolved parent 9650. If the subtype is stated (NS, MC, LR, LD, NLPHL) use the specific entry. Caution: HTLV-1 testing is advised in classic Hodgkin lymphoma with atypical background lymphoid cells — ATLL (9827) can masquerade as classic HL.
Pre-WHO-2001 term, still the wording used in ICD-10 Chapter II (C81.x). Persists in documentation from referring hospitals. Maps to 9650.

Obsolete Jackson-Parker category retained in ICD-O-3 as 9661 and therefore present in the REDCap dropdown. It is NOT a current diagnosis: a modern report describing classic Hodgkin lymphoma should be coded 9650-9655 or 9663. Use 9661 only when the report itself says 'Hodgkin granuloma'.

Parent NOS code 9650. The commonest paediatric subtype is nodular sclerosis (9663) in high-income settings but MIXED CELLULARITY (9652) in sub-Saharan Africa — do not treat nodular sclerosis as the default here. If the report names a subtype, use that entry instead. Before any code is emitted the tree runs the not-lymphoma gate: FNAC misses about 1 in 5 Hodgkin lymphomas (false-negative rate 22.2%), and in a high-TB setting a child with a peripheral node is roughly fourteen times more likely to have mycobacterial disease than cancer.

The rarest classic HL subtype (9653), associated with advanced-stage disease and with HIV — relevant in this setting. The older sub-variants diffuse fibrosis (9654) and reticular (9655) are essentially never distinguished in current practice; 9653 NOS is the default.

Classic HL with an abundant small-lymphocyte background (9651). Uncommon. MUST be distinguished from NLPHL (9659) and from T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma (9688) — the three sit on one morphological triangle and have different biology and treatment. CD30+/CD15+ with weak PAX5 and CD20-negative-to-weak favours 9651.

9652. The commonest classic HL subtype in sub-Saharan African children and in young children generally, and the most EBV-associated: expected EBER positivity 70-80%, so a positive EBER here is expected and weakly informative rather than diagnostic.

Lacunar cells and collagen bands. The commonest classic HL subtype in adolescents and in high-income settings (9663). Note that mixed cellularity (9652) predominates in sub-Saharan African children, so nodular sclerosis is not the default here. Grading (grade 1 = 9665, grade 2 = 9667, cellular phase = 9664) is possible but rarely stated in routine reports; 9663 NOS is the normal answer.

BNLI grade 2 (lymphocyte-depleted) nodular sclerosis (9667). Rarely reported; use 9663 when the grade is not stated.

Dual-group code 9823: Group I (Ia2, CLL) if C42.x blood/marrow; Group II (IIb2, SLL) if nodal. confidence=low: the alias alone cannot settle the group — topography does. Extremely rare in children.

also_known_as: B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma
notes: Combined abbreviation, code 9823. Dual-group code 9823: Group I (Ia2, CLL) if C42.x blood/marrow; Group II (IIb2, SLL) if nodal.

full_form: Crosti's disease -> Primary cutaneous follicle centre lymphoma (9597)
notes: Eponym (reticulohistiocytoma of the dorsum, Crosti 1951) for primary cutaneous follicle centre lymphoma presenting on the back. Maps to 9597.

full_form: Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS (9680)
notes: The commonest aggressive NHL worldwide, code 9680; the Layer 1 / REDCap option string is 'Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS'. In a child, DLBCL NOS must be separated from Burkitt lymphoma (9687): CD10, BCL6, BCL2, MYC and Ki-67 do the work — BCL2-negative with Ki-67 at or above 90% favours Burkitt. In localised paediatric head-and-neck disease the tree attaches a visible provisional: large B-cell lymphoma with IRF4 rearrangement occupies the same site and age, has no code, and NHL-BFM DE-ESCALATES for it — over-coding drives over-treatment.

full_form: Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS (9680)
notes: Code 9680. Use when no DLBCL subtype or genetic lesion is stated. In a child, DLBCL NOS must be separated from Burkitt lymphoma (9687): CD10, BCL6, BCL2, MYC and Ki-67 do the work — BCL2-negative with Ki-67 at or above 90% favours Burkitt.

alias: Diffuse mixed small and large cell lymphoma
full_form: Malignant lymphoma, mixed small and large cell, diffuse (9675)
notes: Working Formulation wording for 9675. Archival — see the full ICD-O-3 term entry. This is a Working Formulation PATTERN, not a WHO entity: a modern report describing this picture would classify it as DLBCL (9680), follicular lymphoma grade 3 (9698) or a T-cell lymphoma. Use 9675 only when the report itself uses this wording.

High-frequency abbreviation, code 9680. If the report specifies the immunoblastic variant use 9684; if T-cell/histiocyte-rich, 9688; if intravascular, 9712; if mediastinal, 9679. In a child, DLBCL NOS must be separated from Burkitt lymphoma (9687): CD10, BCL6, BCL2, MYC and Ki-67 do the work — BCL2-negative with Ki-67 at or above 90% favours Burkitt.

Abbreviation with the NOS qualifier spelled out. Code 9680. Use when no DLBCL subtype or genetic lesion is stated. In a child, separate it from Burkitt lymphoma (9687) with CD10, BCL6, BCL2, MYC and Ki-67 before accepting the code.

full_form: DLBCL with MYC and BCL2 protein co-expression -> Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS (9680)
notes: IMMUNOHISTOCHEMICAL co-expression of MYC and BCL2 protein — a prognostic descriptor, NOT a genetic diagnosis and NOT the same thing as double-hit. It has no code and does not change the code: 9680. Recording it as double-hit would overstate the evidence.

full_form: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements -> Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS (9680)
notes: Clinical shorthand for HGBL with concurrent MYC and BCL2 (with or without BCL6) rearrangements. No ICD-O-3 code; falls back to 9680 with the FISH result preserved. Requires FISH — MYC IHC is NOT a FISH surrogate: dual-expressor pre-selection at 40% misses about 35% of double-hit cases and at 70% still misses 10-15%. nci_concept_id null.

full_form: EBV-positive DLBCL, NOS -> Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS (9680)
notes: Abbreviated form. Codes 9680; requires over 80% EBER-positive malignant cells. nci_concept_id null. A few scattered EBER-positive cells do not qualify — in this population scattered positivity is close to the background state. There is no separate ICD-O-3 code; capture eber_status against 9680.

full_form: EBV-positive DLBCL, NOS -> Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS (9680)
notes: Requires MORE THAN 80% of viable malignant cells to be EBER-positive — a few scattered EBER-positive cells do not qualify, and in this population scattered positivity is the background state. No separate ICD-O-3 code; codes 9680 with eber_status captured. nci_concept_id null.

Plasmacytoma arising outside bone and marrow, code 9734; commonest in the upper aerodigestive tract. Must be separated from osseous plasmacytoma (9731), from myeloma (9732) and — in an HIV-positive patient — from plasmablastic lymphoma (9735), which is CD20-negative with a high Ki-67.

alias: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue
full_form: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of MALT -> Marginal zone B-cell lymphoma, NOS (9699)
notes: Full WHO name for MALT lymphoma. Codes 9699. There is no separate MALT code in this code set. Rare in children; commonest sites are stomach, ocular adnexa, salivary gland and thyroid, on a background of chronic antigenic stimulation. Splenic disease codes 9689.

Abbreviation, code 9690 NOS. If a grade is stated use 9695 (grade 1), 9691 (grade 2) or 9698 (grade 3) — but record which grading system the pathologist used, because WHO-HAEM5 merges grades 1+2+3A and makes grading optional while ICC retains 1-2 / 3A / 3B. Ki-67 is explicitly NOT part of grading.

full_form: Follicular large B-cell lymphoma -> Follicular lymphoma, grade 3 (9698)
notes: The WHO-HAEM5 RENAME of follicular lymphoma grade 3B — same code, 9698, arriving as a differently worded report. This alias exists so the clerk can find the 'Follicular lymphoma, grade 3' row from the new wording.

NOS code 9690. CRITICAL PAEDIATRIC RULE: do NOT grade a paediatric follicular lesion by adult rules. Paediatric-type follicular lymphoma looks high-grade — expanded serpiginous follicles of monotonous centroblasts, starry sky — and is indolent and cured by conservative management; mis-grading it as 9698 drives inappropriate intensive chemotherapy. PTFL is BCL2-NEGATIVE with BCL2-R, BCL6-R, MYC-R and IRF4-R all absent.

Code 9695. Record which grading system the pathologist used — WHO-HAEM5 merges grades 1, 2 and 3A as classic FL and makes grading optional; ICC retains 1-2 / 3A / 3B. Without that, the grade field is uninterpretable. In a child, do not grade at all — see the paediatric-type follicular lymphoma entry.

Code 9691. Record the grading system used. Do not grade paediatric follicular lesions. WHO-HAEM5 merges grades 1, 2 and 3A as classic FL with grading optional, while ICC retains 1-2 / 3A / 3B — without the classification system recorded, the grade field is uninterpretable. Ki-67 is explicitly not part of grading.

Code 9698, covering ICC grade 3A and 3B and WHO-HAEM5's 'follicular large B-cell lymphoma'. Record the grading system used. CRITICAL: in a child, a high-grade-looking follicular lesion is far more likely to be paediatric-type FL (code 9690, ungraded) — mis-grading it here drives inappropriate intensive chemotherapy.

The Layer 1 / REDCap option string verbatim for 9690. Use when no grade is stated. In a child do not grade at all: paediatric-type FL is BCL2-negative, indolent and cured conservatively, and mis-grading it as 9698 drives inappropriate intensive chemotherapy.

Clonal B-cell/plasma cell disorder secreting a truncated immunoglobulin heavy chain with no light chain, code 9762 (gamma, mu and alpha types). The ALPHA type is immunoproliferative small intestinal disease and has its own code, 9764. Not a paediatric entity.

full_form: High-Grade B-Cell Lymphoma -> Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS (9680)
notes: Abbreviation for high-grade B-cell lymphoma. Falls back to 9680 with the genetics captured as free text; never 9687. nci_concept_id null.

full_form: High-Grade B-Cell Lymphoma, Double Hit -> Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS (9680)
notes: Abbreviation for double-hit high-grade B-cell lymphoma. Falls back to 9680; FISH-dependent. nci_concept_id null.

full_form: HHV8-positive DLBCL, NOS -> Large B-cell lymphoma arising in HHV8-associated multicentric Castleman disease (9738)
notes: WHO-HAEM5 wording for the entity carried by 9738. HHV-8 LANA-1 is DEFINITIONAL — 9678 and 9738 cannot be assigned without it. Document HIV status.

full_form: High-grade B-cell lymphoma -> Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS (9680)
notes: Uncoded-entity fallback (Pathway 5.2): HGBL-MYC/BCL2 (with or without BCL6) and HGBL NOS have no ICD-O-3 code and fall back to 9680, with the genetics preserved as free text. Do NOT code them 9687 — a MYC rearrangement alone does not make a case Burkitt. nci_concept_id null: the Group II session recorded no NCIt ID for this umbrella term.

full_form: High-grade B-cell lymphoma, NOS -> Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS (9680)
notes: WHO-HAEM5 category with no ICD-O-3 code; falls back to 9680 (Pathway 5.2). nci_concept_id null. Do NOT code it 9687 — a MYC rearrangement alone does not make a case Burkitt. Preserve the genetics as free text against 9680 or the information is lost permanently.

full_form: Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, immunoblastic, NOS (9684)
notes: Fuller wording for 9684. See the 'Immunoblastic lymphoma' entry. Requires over 90% immunoblasts. Most current reports will simply say DLBCL (9680); use 9684 only when the report says immunoblastic. In an HIV-positive patient, exclude plasmablastic lymphoma (9735) first.

full_form: Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, immunoblastic, NOS (9684)
notes: Morphological variant of DLBCL with over 90% immunoblasts, code 9684. WHO no longer requires the variant to be reported, so most current reports will say DLBCL (9680); use 9684 only when the report says immunoblastic. In an HIV-positive patient an immunoblastic/plasmablastic picture should prompt exclusion of plasmablastic lymphoma (9735).
Kiel-classification term for lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma. Maps to 9671. Appears in older European-trained reporting.
Code 9769. Deposition of monoclonal light or heavy chains in tissue, usually kidney, from an underlying plasma cell clone. Not a paediatric entity; carried because the code is in the REDCap dropdown.

Code 9764. A MALT-type lymphoma of the small bowel secreting truncated alpha heavy chain; occurs in adolescents in low-income settings with high enteric infection burden, so it is not impossible in this registry. Early-stage disease can respond to antibiotics.

DLBCL variant in which the tumour cells are confined to small-vessel lumina, code 9712. Presents with organ dysfunction, fever and cytopenias rather than lymphadenopathy, so it is usually diagnosed on a random skin or marrow biopsy. Extremely rare in children.

Abbreviation for immunoproliferative small intestinal disease (9764). A MALT-type lymphoma of the small bowel secreting truncated alpha heavy chain, in adolescents and young adults in settings with a high enteric infection burden. Alpha heavy chain disease codes here, not 9762. Early-stage disease can respond to antibiotics.

Abbreviation for intravascular large B-cell lymphoma (9712). The tumour cells are confined to small-vessel lumina; the presentation is organ dysfunction, fever and cytopenias rather than lymphadenopathy, so the diagnosis is usually made on a random skin or marrow biopsy. Extremely rare in children.
Historical eponym for multiple myeloma, after Otto Kahler. Rarely used in modern practice but appears in older East African medical texts. Maps to 9732.

full_form: Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS (9680)
notes: Generic descriptive term. Defaults to 9680, but the tree must first exclude the coded large B-cell entities that have their own codes: 9679 mediastinal, 9678 primary effusion, 9688 T-cell/histiocyte-rich, 9712 intravascular, 9735 plasmablastic, 9737 ALK-positive, 9738 HHV8/Castleman-associated.

alias: Large B-cell lymphoma arising in HHV8-associated multicentric Castleman disease
full_form: Large B-cell lymphoma arising in HHV8-associated multicentric Castleman disease (9738)
notes: The Layer 1 / REDCap option string verbatim, code 9738. HHV-8 LANA-1 is DEFINITIONAL — 9678 and 9738 cannot be assigned without it. Document HIV status. Phenotype: LANA-1 positive, cytoplasmic IgM lambda, CD138 NEGATIVE, in a background of multicentric Castleman disease — CD138-negativity is what separates it from 9678. Castleman disease WITHOUT this lymphoma is a non-reportable exit, not a cancer.
Abbreviation, code 9970. Work through the non-reportable exclusions first — most lymphoid proliferations that reach this term are not neoplasms.

Abbreviation for lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma (9671). If an IgM paraprotein is documented, consider 9761. Low-grade B-cell NHL with plasmacytic differentiation; the Layer 1 / REDCap option string is 'Malignant lymphoma, lymphoplasmacytic'. Rare in children.

Abbreviation for lymphomatoid granulomatosis, code 9766 — whose REDCap option string is the archaic 'Angiocentric immunoproliferative lesion'. Lung involvement is definitional; capture the grade, because it decides the drug class.

THE MODERN NAME FOR 9766. The Layer 1 / REDCap option string is the archaic ICD-O-3 term 'Angiocentric immunoproliferative lesion', which no clerk will recognise and which no report will use — this alias is the only place the modern term exists, and the clerk must still select the archaic row in REDCap. An EBV-driven angiocentric, angiodestructive B-cell proliferation. LUNG INVOLVEMENT IS REQUIRED BY DEFINITION (100% of cases); nodal or marrow involvement should raise suspicion of an alternative diagnosis. Grading is by EBER-positive cells per high-power field (grade 1 under 5, grade 2 5-20, grade 3 over 50) and DETERMINES DRUG CLASS — IFN-alpha2b for grades 1-2, DA-EPOCH-R for grade 3 — so grade must be captured as a variable; ICD-O-3 has no grade modifier. Under ICD-O-3.2, 9766/3 is restricted to grade 3. Grade may change in either direction on re-biopsy WITHOUT a new primary.

full_form: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis grade 3 -> Angiocentric immunoproliferative lesion (9766)
notes: Grade 3 LYG — over 50 and often over 100 EBER-positive cells per high-power field. Under ICD-O-3.2 this is the grade to which 9766/3 is restricted, and it is the grade treated with DA-EPOCH-R rather than interferon. Code 9766 with grade captured as a variable.

Low-grade B-cell NHL with plasmacytic differentiation, code 9671 — the Layer 1 / REDCap option string is 'Malignant lymphoma, lymphoplasmacytic'. When an IgM paraprotein is present the entity is Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia (9761). Rare in children.

Catch-all code 9970 for a lymphoid proliferation that cannot be shown to be a defined lymphoma. Use only after the tree's non-reportable inventory has been worked through — reactive hyperplasia, TB lymphadenitis, HIV-associated PGL, Castleman disease, infectious mononucleosis and IgG4-related disease all exit as NOT REPORTABLE rather than to 9970.

alias: Malignant lymphoma, mixed small and large cell, diffuse
full_form: Malignant lymphoma, mixed small and large cell, diffuse (9675)
also_known_as: Diffuse Mixed Large and Small Cell Lymphoma
notes: Working Formulation era pattern description retained as ICD-O-3 code 9675 and present in the REDCap dropdown. It is NOT a current WHO entity — a modern report describing this picture would classify it as DLBCL (9680), follicular lymphoma grade 3 (9698) or a T-cell lymphoma. Use 9675 only when the report itself uses this wording.

full_form: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue -> Marginal zone B-cell lymphoma, NOS (9699)
notes: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue. Codes 9699 in this code set. Rare in children; commonest sites stomach, ocular adnexa, salivary gland and thyroid, usually on a background of chronic antigenic stimulation.

Aggressive B-cell NHL defined by t(11;14) and cyclin D1 overexpression, code 9673. Very rare in children — a paediatric 'mantle cell lymphoma' should be reviewed before acceptance. Note that DLBCL with a CCND1 rearrangement codes 9680, NOT 9673 (Pathway 5.2).

full_form: Mantle zone lymphoma -> Mantle cell lymphoma (9673)
notes: Older name for mantle cell lymphoma. Maps to 9673. Defined by t(11;14) and cyclin D1 overexpression. Very rare in children — review a paediatric case before accepting it. Note that DLBCL with a CCND1 rearrangement codes 9680, not 9673.

The Layer 1 / REDCap option string verbatim for 9699. Covers extranodal (MALT) and nodal marginal zone lymphoma; splenic MZL has its own code, 9689. In a child, paediatric nodal MZL belongs on the paediatric-type follicular lymphoma spectrum and codes 9690, not here.

NOS code 9699, covering extranodal (MALT) and nodal marginal zone lymphoma. Splenic MZL has its own code, 9689. MNDA and IRTA1 favour marginal zone over follicular when CD10 is negative and BCL2 ambiguous. In a child, check first whether the report describes paediatric nodal MZL — that belongs on the PTFL spectrum and codes 9690, not 9699.

Abbreviation for mantle cell lymphoma (9673). CAUTION: 'MCL' is also written for MAST CELL LEUKAEMIA (9742) and occasionally for mixed cellularity Hodgkin lymphoma — read the surrounding report before accepting this mapping. Extremely rare in paediatrics.

The Layer 1 / REDCap option string verbatim for 9679. Thymic B-cell origin, in adolescents and young adults, more often female. CD23 (positive in 75%) is the marker most panels omit. Clinical alert: airway and SVC obstruction with an anterior mediastinal mass.

Abbreviation, code 9765. Pre-malignant, not a malignancy — see the full-name entry before registering it. Progression risk is about 1% per year. It is carried only because the code exists in the REDCap dropdown and can appear as an initial diagnosis before progression; a paediatric MGUS should be reviewed before it is registered as a cancer.
Abbreviation for multiple myeloma (9732). CAUTION: 'MM' is also written for malignant melanoma — read the report before accepting. Not a paediatric entity.

Pre-malignant plasma cell condition, code 9765. It is NOT itself a malignancy — it is carried because it can appear in registry files as an initial diagnosis before progression, and because the code exists in the REDCap dropdown. Progression risk about 1% per year. Essentially not a paediatric entity; a paediatric MGUS should be reviewed before it is registered as a cancer.

full_form: Monomorphic post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder -> code to the specific lymphoma (9971 only if unclassifiable)
notes: TRAP: under ICD-O-3.2 monomorphic PTLD codes to the SPECIFIC LYMPHOMA it resembles — most often DLBCL (9680) or Burkitt (9687) — not to 9971. 9971 is the fallback only when the specific entity cannot be established. confidence=low for that reason.

Plasma cell neoplasm, code 9732. Virtually unheard of in children — a paediatric 'myeloma' should be reviewed. The definitional threshold that closes the fork against plasmablastic lymphoma (9735): 10% or more clonal bone-marrow plasma cells OR a biopsy-proven plasmacytoma, PLUS at least one myeloma-defining event (CRAB — hypercalcaemia, renal insufficiency, anaemia, lytic bone lesions — or an added biomarker of imminent organ damage). Below that threshold the case is not myeloma.
Clinical shorthand for multiple myeloma (9732). If the lesion is solitary, use plasmacytoma (9731) or extramedullary plasmacytoma (9734) instead.

Abbreviation, code 9699 NOS. If splenic, use 9689. Covers MALT and nodal marginal zone lymphoma. MNDA and IRTA1 favour marginal zone over follicular when CD10 is negative and BCL2 ambiguous. A paediatric nodal MZL belongs on the PTFL spectrum and codes 9690.

full_form: Nodal marginal zone lymphoma -> Marginal zone B-cell lymphoma, NOS (9699)
notes: Codes 9699 in adults. IN A CHILD, do not accept this at face value: paediatric nodal marginal zone lymphoma is part of the PTFL spectrum and codes 9690 (Pathway 5.2).

full_form: Paediatric nodal marginal zone lymphoma -> Follicular lymphoma, NOS (9690)
notes: TRAP: paediatric nodal marginal zone lymphoma is now regarded as part of the PTFL spectrum and falls back to 9690, NOT to 9699 (Pathway 5.2). Auto-coding a pNMZL referral to marginal zone lymphoma is the specific error this entry prevents. Conservative management. nci_concept_id null.

full_form: Paediatric-type follicular lymphoma -> Follicular lymphoma, NOS (9690)
notes: P0 uncoded entity (Pathway 5.2): PTFL has no ICD-O-3 code and falls back to 9690 with a paediatric flag — and it must NOT BE GRADED. It is BCL2-negative with no BCL2, BCL6, MYC or IRF4 rearrangement, and is cured by conservative management despite high-grade-looking morphology. Coding it 9698 is the error this entry exists to prevent. nci_concept_id null: no NCIt ID was recorded for this entity in the Group II session.
Abbreviation for plasmablastic lymphoma (9735). HIV testing is mandatory. Caution: 'PBL' is also written for peripheral blood lymphocytes — read the context.

Abbreviation for primary cutaneous follicle centre lymphoma (9597). B-cell, indolent. Indolent with an excellent prognosis, and it routes through the MAIN tree rather than the cutaneous T-cell tree because it is a B-cell entity. A systemic follicular lymphoma with skin involvement is 9690, not 9597.

full_form: Pediatric-type follicular lymphoma -> Follicular lymphoma, NOS (9690)
notes: US spelling of paediatric-type follicular lymphoma. Codes 9690 with a paediatric flag; do not grade. nci_concept_id null.
Abbreviation for primary effusion lymphoma (9678). HHV-8 LANA-1 is DEFINITIONAL — 9678 and 9738 cannot be assigned without it. Document HIV status.

UK spelling. Maps to 9733; the REDCap option row uses the US spelling. The leukaemic phase of a plasma cell neoplasm, primary (de novo) or secondary to myeloma. Not a paediatric entity; 9733 sits in ICCC-3 IIb2 because the subgroup follows the ICD-O code, not the clinical presentation.

Leukaemic phase of a plasma cell neoplasm, code 9733; primary (de novo) or secondary (from myeloma). Not a paediatric entity — carried for registry completeness. A leukaemic presentation would normally place the case in Group I; 9733 sits in ICCC-3 IIb2 because the subgroup follows the ICD-O code.

Aggressive B-cell lymphoma with plasmablastic morphology, code 9735; common in the oral cavity and strongly HIV-associated. Phenotype CD20-negative, CD138+, MUM1+, BLIMP1+, CD38+, PAX5-negative, Ki-67 high, LANA-1 NEGATIVE (a positive LANA-1 makes it 9678 or 9738). EBER is supportive, not definitional — an EBER-negative case is still PBL — and LMP1 IHC must NOT be used here. Clinical alert: HIV antibody and viral load are mandatory; SPEP, immunofixation, skeletal survey and a marrow are required to EXONERATE myeloma before 9735 is closed. Note the warning that applies directly to this registry: HIV infection and younger age do not by themselves support a diagnosis of PBL in a high-HIV-burden country.

Solitary plasma cell tumour, code 9731. If extramedullary (outside bone), use 9734. If there are multiple lesions or the marrow shows 10% or more clonal plasma cells with a myeloma-defining event, the case is multiple myeloma (9732).

Commonest abbreviation for primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma (9679). Also written PMBL. Distinguish from T-LBL (9837) and from nodular sclerosis classic HL (9663), which share the anterior mediastinal presentation in adolescents.

Alternative abbreviation for 9679. Also written PMBCL. Distinguish from T-LBL (9837) and from nodular sclerosis classic Hodgkin lymphoma (9663), which share the anterior mediastinal presentation in adolescents. Clinical alert: airway and SVC obstruction.
Polymorphic PTLD is 9971 and is coded /1 under ICD-O-3.2, which places it outside ICCC-3 Group II. The behaviour is resolved in the tree, not by the alias.

Lymphoid proliferation after solid-organ or stem-cell transplantation, code 9971 — the Layer 1 / REDCap option string is 'Post transplant lymphoproliferative disorder, NOS' (no hyphen). Tissue biopsy with WHO classification is the gold standard: EBV DNA LOAD IS A SCREENING AND MONITORING TOOL, NOT A DIAGNOSTIC ONE, and cannot on its own reach 9971. A material proportion of PTLD is EBV-NEGATIVE, so a negative EBER does not exclude it — and a small number of EBV-positive cells in a graft recipient is not by itself evidence of PTLD. Under ICD-O-3.2 polymorphic PTLD is 9971/1 and MONOMORPHIC PTLD CODES TO THE SPECIFIC LYMPHOMA, not to 9971. Where paediatric solid-organ transplantation is not performed, a populated 9971 warrants review before acceptance.

full_form: Primary diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the CNS -> Malignant lymphoma, large B-cell, diffuse, NOS (9680)
notes: Primary CNS lymphoma is a large B-cell lymphoma and codes 9680, staying in ICCC-3 Group II (IIb2) — ICCC-3 assigns lymphomas by MORPHOLOGY, so a C71 topography does not move the case to Group III. Rare in children outside immunodeficiency; check HIV status.

Indolent B-CELL lymphoma of the skin, code 9597, with an excellent prognosis. Note it is a B-cell entity and therefore routes through the MAIN tree, not the cutaneous T-cell tree. Distinct from systemic follicular lymphoma (9690) — a systemic FL with skin involvement is 9690, not 9597.

HHV-8-driven large B-cell lymphoma presenting as a serous effusion without a tumour mass, code 9678. HHV-8 LANA-1 is DEFINITIONAL — 9678 and 9738 cannot be assigned without it. Document HIV status. Phenotype CD138+, CD20-negative, with EBER positive in 75-90% (supportive, not definitional). An extracavitary/solid variant exists and will look anomalous against the code name. Almost always HIV-associated.

Thymic B-cell origin, code 9679; the Layer 1 / REDCap option string is 'Mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma'. Occurs in adolescents and young adults, more often female. Phenotype BCL6+ 96%, MUM1+ 82%, CD30+ 88%, CD23+ 75% — CD23 is the marker most panels omit. In paediatric mature B-cell lymphoma PMBCL is the least common of Burkitt / germinal-centre DLBCL / PMBCL overall, but the most likely of the three once the mass is anterior mediastinal and the patient adolescent. Clinical alert: airway and SVC obstruction.

full_form: Paediatric-Type Follicular Lymphoma -> Follicular lymphoma, NOS (9690)
notes: Abbreviation for paediatric-type follicular lymphoma. Codes 9690, ungraded. nci_concept_id null. It has no ICD-O-3 code of its own and must NOT be graded — BCL2-negative with BCL2, BCL6, MYC and IRF4 rearrangements all absent, and cured by conservative management despite high-grade-looking morphology.
Abbreviation, code 9971. Document EBV status, but do not use EBV DNA load as the diagnosis. Non-destructive PTLD is a non-reportable exit; monomorphic PTLD codes to the specific lymphoma.

Abbreviation for small lymphocytic lymphoma (9670). If the report writes 'CLL/SLL' as one entity, use 9823 instead. Coded in Group II when nodal; coded in Group I only when blood or marrow involvement is documented.

full_form: Malignant lymphoma, small B lymphocytic, NOS (9670)
notes: The nodal counterpart of CLL, code 9670 — the Layer 1 / REDCap option string is 'Malignant lymphoma, small B lymphocytic, NOS'. Use when the presentation is lymphadenopathy without significant blood involvement. The combined CLL/SLL entity has its own code, 9823. Very rare in paediatrics.

Abbreviation for splenic marginal zone lymphoma (9689). Very rare in paediatrics. Splenomegaly with circulating villous lymphocytes; a separate code from MZL NOS (9699). Note that the spleen is C42.2 and is therefore a Group II topography even though it is a haematopoietic organ.
Osseous solitary plasmacytoma, code 9731. Requires a negative skeletal survey and a marrow below the myeloma threshold.

also_known_as: Splenic Lymphoma with Circulating Villous Lymphocytes
notes: Marginal zone lymphoma arising in the spleen, with its own code 9689 — separate from MZL NOS (9699). Splenomegaly with circulating villous lymphocytes. Rare in children; note that the spleen is C42.2 and therefore a Group II topography even though it is a haematopoietic organ.

Older name, before 'histiocyte-rich' was added. Maps to 9688. Scattered CD20-positive neoplastic B cells in a dense reactive T-cell and histiocyte background — the aggressive member of the NLPHL / LRCHL / THRLBCL triangle. IHC is required; the case can also mimic a peripheral T-cell lymphoma.

A DLBCL variant in which scattered large neoplastic B cells sit in a dense background of T cells and histiocytes, code 9688. It is the aggressive member of the NLPHL / LRCHL / THRLBCL triangle and can mimic both — and can also mimic a peripheral T-cell lymphoma, because most of the cells present are reactive T cells. IHC is required; the neoplastic cells are CD20+ and CD30-/CD15-.
Abbreviation for T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma (9688). Distinguish from NLPHL (9659) — same morphological family, opposite prognosis.

The WHO name carries '(thymic)' in parentheses; some reports use it alone. Maps to 9679. Phenotype BCL6+ 96%, MUM1+ 82%, CD30+ 88%, CD23+ 75% — CD23 is the marker most panels omit. Clinical alert: airway and SVC obstruction with an anterior mediastinal mass.
UK spelling ('-aemia'), standard in East African reporting. Maps to 9761; the REDCap option row uses the US spelling.

Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma with an IgM paraprotein, code 9761 — the Layer 1 / REDCap option string is spelled without the umlaut, which is what the clerk must select. Named for Jan G. Waldenstrom. Essentially unheard of in children; carried for registry completeness.

Possessive eponym variant. Maps to 9761. Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma (9671) with an IgM paraprotein. The REDCap option string is spelled without the umlaut and without the possessive, and that is the row the clerk must select. Essentially unheard of in children.

Abbreviation for Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia (9761). Adult entity. Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma (9671) with an IgM paraprotein. Essentially unheard of in children; carried for registry completeness. The REDCap option row is spelled without the umlaut.

UK spelling; the REDCap option row uses the US spelling. HTLV-1 serology is the absolute gate and is MANDATORY — without it the code is unassignable and the case falls back to 9702. The leukaemic variant of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, code 9701 — the REDCap option string is spelled without the accent. Triad of erythroderma, generalised lymphadenopathy and circulating Sezary cells. 9701 IS DEFINITIONALLY CLINICAL PLUS HAEMATOLOGICAL PLUS MOLECULAR — A PATHOLOGY REPORT CAN NEVER ESTABLISH IT ALONE, and the skin biopsy is non-specific in as many as a third of cases, so a negative biopsy does not exclude it. Requires an identical T-cell clone in blood and skin plus one blood threshold (Sezary count over 1000/microlitre, or CD4/CD8 ratio 10 or more, or CD4+CD7-negative at least 40%, or CD4+CD26-negative at least 30%). Code 9708. Subcutaneous nodules and plaques; ALPHA-BETA lineage — BETA-F1 POSITIVE — CD8+, CD4-negative, CD56 NEGATIVE, cytotoxic proteins positive, EBV negative. Five-year disease-specific survival 87%. The one antibody pair that separates it from primary cutaneous gamma-delta T-cell lymphoma (9726, survival 11%) is betaF1 plus CD56; without them a lobular panniculitic infiltrate cannot be coded beyond 9702. That survival gap is the largest consequence of a single stain anywhere in this group. A subset of REACTIVE T cells in SPTCL expresses TCR gamma-delta, so a gamma-delta population is not by itself sufficient for 9726 — the gamma-delta cells must be the neoplastic ones. HLH drives the poor outcomes within this otherwise favourable entity; germline HAVCR2 mutation in about 25%. Note 9708 routes through the MAIN tree, not the cutaneous tree.

Historical eponym for MULTIFOCAL Langerhans cell histiocytosis — the classic triad of lytic skull lesions, exophthalmos and diabetes insipidus. Maps to 9754, the code replacing the former disseminated LCH codes. Under ICD-O-3.2 the behaviour of 9751 turns on EXTENT: unifocal, single-system multifocal or single-system pulmonary disease is /1 — outside ICCC-3 Group II — and multisystem disease (two or more organs or organ systems) is /3. That call is established by vertex-to-toes FDG-PET/CT; a skull-to-mid-thigh scan is explicitly inadequate. Without PET-CT the tool defaults to 9751 with an extent_unknown flag rather than guessing, and records what imaging was actually done — the realistic substitute (skeletal survey plus abdominal ultrasound plus chest X-ray) will UNDER-CALL multisystem disease and bias cases out of Group II. Clinical alert: diabetes insipidus needs hormone replacement regardless of focality.

full_form: Congenital self-healing reticulohistiocytosis -> Langerhans cell histiocytosis, NOS (9751)
notes: Congenital self-healing reticulohistiocytosis — the neonatal skin-limited form of LCH, which regresses spontaneously. Maps to 9751; as single-system disease it is 9751/1 and falls outside ICCC-3 Group II. The behaviour is resolved in the tree by extent, and a self-healing course does not by itself settle it — staging is still required.

Scott-Robb-Smith 1939 term, an NCIt synonym for malignant histiocytosis. Maps to 9750. Most cases described under this name would today be anaplastic large cell lymphoma (9714) or a T/NK-cell lymphoma with haemophagocytosis — review before accepting.

Code 9755: CD163-POSITIVE plus at least one further macrophage/monocyte marker (CD68, CD4, CD14), with overt malignant cytology. S100 MAY BE PATCHY-POSITIVE in 9755 — do not read a positive S100 as excluding it; read CD1a and CD207 for that. Required panel on every suspected histiocytic case: CD163, CD1a, CD207/langerin and S100, with at least two lineage-specific markers expressed on the malignant cells. LCH is S100+, CD1a+, CD207+ with DIFFUSE staining, grooved reniform nuclei and a CD68 Golgi dot. CD1a ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT — it mistakes an indeterminate dendritic cell tumour for LCH. PU.1 is the tie-breaker in hard cases and in excluding undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma. IN CHILDREN SPECIFICALLY: histiocytic sarcoma following acute leukaemia or lymphoma is MORE common than in adults — published paediatric cases show 82% male, mean age 6.6 years, presenting during ALL maintenance, bone the commonest site (65%). A histiocytic tumour in a child on ALL maintenance is a second-primary-versus-transdifferentiation decision BY DEFAULT, so prior_haematopoietic_malignancy is a required field here.

full_form: Histiocytosis X -> Langerhans cell histiocytosis, NOS (9751)
notes: Historical umbrella term replaced by 'Langerhans cell histiocytosis' in the 1990s — the 'X' denoted unknown aetiology. It covered eosinophilic granuloma, Hand-Schuller-Christian disease and Letterer-Siwe disease. Persists in older clinical literature and East African textbooks. Maps to 9751.

The Layer 1 / REDCap option string verbatim for 9741. Adopt the harmonized 2024 criteria: systemic mastocytosis requires 1 major plus 1 minor criterion, or 3 minor. ICC's position that the major criterion alone suffices is a live conflict, so criteria_set_used must be captured or ICC-diagnosed cases will be silently miscoded. Minor criteria: over 25% atypical or spindled mast cells; an activating KIT mutation at codon 816 or another critical region; CD2 and/or CD25 AND/OR CD30 (CD30 is new — a legacy CD25-only panel misses well-differentiated SM entirely); basal serum tryptase at or above 20 ng/mL.

Code 9757: S100-POSITIVE, CD1a-NEGATIVE, CD207-NEGATIVE, melanocytic markers negative, with PU.1 recommended. S100 IS WHAT SEPARATES 9757 FROM 9755 — but a weak or patchy S100 does not by itself make the case 9757, because patchy S100 is expected in histiocytic sarcoma. MELANOMA MUST BE EXCLUDED: this entity lacks any defining marker of its own.

Abbreviation, code 9741. Requires a marrow. Systemic mastocytosis requires 1 major plus 1 minor criterion, or 3 minor, under the harmonized 2024 criteria — and it requires a MARROW. Do not code 9741 on skin findings alone; a skin-only case is 'mastocytosis in the skin' and is formally unclassified.

NCIt synonym and an older name for LCH. Maps to 9751. Under ICD-O-3.2 the behaviour of 9751 turns on extent — unifocal or single-system disease is /1 and falls outside ICCC-3 Group II, multisystem disease is /3. Without vertex-to-toes PET-CT the tool defaults to 9751 with an extent_unknown flag.

Clonal proliferation of Langerhans cells and a significant paediatric entity. Presentation ranges from a single bone lesion to multisystem disease. Code 9751 for NOS; 9754 is the code that replaces the former disseminated codes. Required panel on every suspected histiocytic case: CD163, CD1a, CD207/langerin and S100, with at least two lineage-specific markers expressed on the malignant cells. LCH is S100+, CD1a+, CD207+ with DIFFUSE staining, grooved reniform nuclei and a CD68 Golgi dot. CD1a ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT — it mistakes an indeterminate dendritic cell tumour for LCH. Under ICD-O-3.2 the behaviour of 9751 turns on EXTENT: unifocal, single-system multifocal or single-system pulmonary disease is /1 — outside ICCC-3 Group II — and multisystem disease (two or more organs or organ systems) is /3. That call is established by vertex-to-toes FDG-PET/CT; a skull-to-mid-thigh scan is explicitly inadequate. Without PET-CT the tool defaults to 9751 with an extent_unknown flag rather than guessing, and records what imaging was actually done — the realistic substitute (skeletal survey plus abdominal ultrasound plus chest X-ray) will UNDER-CALL multisystem disease and bias cases out of Group II. MAPK-pathway mutations, most often BRAF V600E, are found in most cases and are treatment-changing; VE1 IHC alone is not sufficiently sensitive or specific, so record the assay used. Clinical alert: LCH with diabetes insipidus needs hormone replacement regardless of focality.

Code 9756: S100+, CD1a+, CD207+ WITH OVERTLY MALIGNANT CYTOLOGY. The CD1a and CD207 staining may be PATCHY here, unlike LCH's diffuse pattern. Required panel on every suspected histiocytic case: CD163, CD1a, CD207/langerin and S100, with at least two lineage-specific markers expressed on the malignant cells. LCH is S100+, CD1a+, CD207+ with DIFFUSE staining, grooved reniform nuclei and a CD68 Golgi dot. CD1a ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT — it mistakes an indeterminate dendritic cell tumour for LCH. Note that mitotic count, atypical mitoses and Ki-67 are explicitly NOT needed for the diagnosis — the requirement is overt malignant cytology, described qualitatively. Under 5% langerin makes the case a high-grade indeterminate dendritic cell tumour, which has no code and must NOT be coded 9756.

High-frequency paediatric-oncology abbreviation. Codes 9751 (NOS) or 9754 (the code replacing the former disseminated codes). Under ICD-O-3.2 the behaviour of 9751 turns on EXTENT: unifocal, single-system multifocal or single-system pulmonary disease is /1 — outside ICCC-3 Group II — and multisystem disease (two or more organs or organ systems) is /3. Without PET-CT the tool defaults to 9751 with an extent_unknown flag rather than guessing, and records what imaging was actually done — the realistic substitute (skeletal survey plus abdominal ultrasound plus chest X-ray) will UNDER-CALL multisystem disease and bias cases out of Group II.

Historical eponym for acute DISSEMINATED Langerhans cell histiocytosis of infancy, with skin, liver, spleen and marrow involvement. Maps to 9754. Multisystem disease is the /3 half and IS reportable in Group II.

The consensus umbrella (MHN) covers histiocytic sarcoma (9755), Langerhans cell sarcoma (9756), interdigitating dendritic cell sarcoma (9757) and high-grade indeterminate dendritic cell tumour (no code) — and EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES LCH, Erdheim-Chester, Rosai-Dorfman, juvenile xanthogranuloma, ALK-positive histiocytosis, FDC sarcoma and fibroblastic reticular cell tumour. Use the specific code where the phenotype allows; 9750 only as the ambiguous endpoint, pending the registrar decision.

Code 9750. The consensus view is that this category historically served as a WASTEBASKET and was removed from WHO in 2016. Only about 52% of cases referred as 'malignant histiocytosis' are confirmed as such on expert review — roughly half of what arrives under this label is something else. DO NOT default an unclassified histiocytic infiltrate here: the consensus endpoint for an ambiguous case is MHN-NOS, which has no ICD-O-3 code. REGISTRAR DECISION OUTSTANDING (Pathway 5.2, 9.3): either 9750 is repurposed as the MHN-NOS carrier with a coding note, or ambiguous cases sit at 9750 while the report says something the code does not mean.

full_form: Mast cell disease -> Mastocytoma, NOS (9740) / Indolent systemic mastocytosis (9741) / Mast cell leukemia (9742)
notes: Descriptive umbrella covering mastocytoma NOS (9740), indolent systemic mastocytosis (9741) and mast cell leukaemia (9742). Routes into the mast cell tree. Adopt the harmonized 2024 criteria: systemic mastocytosis requires 1 major plus 1 minor criterion, or 3 minor. ICC's position that the major criterion alone suffices is a live conflict, so criteria_set_used must be captured or ICC-diagnosed cases will be silently miscoded. Minor criteria: over 25% atypical or spindled mast cells; an activating KIT mutation at codon 816 or another critical region; CD2 and/or CD25 AND/OR CD30 (CD30 is new — a legacy CD25-only panel misses well-differentiated SM entirely); basal serum tryptase at or above 20 ng/mL. KIT D816V is diagnostic — and note the inverted rule: a POSITIVE KIT D816V argues AGAINST mast cell sarcoma. nci_concept_id null: this umbrella phrase has no single NCIt concept, and the specific entities carry their own IDs.

UK spelling; the Layer 1 / REDCap option string uses 'leukemia'. Code 9742 requires 20% OR MORE MAST CELLS ON A MARROW OR PERIPHERAL BLOOD SMEAR — a morphology count achievable anywhere a smear can be read, which makes this one of the few IId codes that does not depend on immunohistochemistry. Note the abbreviation 'MCL' is used for this entity AND for mantle cell lymphoma (9673); this file maps 'MCL' to 9673, so mast cell leukaemia must be typed in full.
The Layer 1 / REDCap option string verbatim for 9742. Requires 20% or more mast cells on a marrow or blood smear.

full_form: Mast cell sarcoma -> Indolent systemic mastocytosis (9741)
notes: Uncoded-entity fallback (Pathway 5.2): no ICD-O-3 code of its own; falls back to 9741 with the subtype as free text. INVERTED RULE WORTH ENCODING: a positive KIT D816V argues AGAINST mast cell sarcoma.

Code 9740, requiring only skin morphology plus tryptase or KIT immunohistochemistry. Solitary mastocytoma versus 2-3 lesions is an explicit lesion-count split. Common and usually benign in young children.

full_form: Mastocytosis -> Mastocytoma, NOS (9740) / Indolent systemic mastocytosis (9741)
notes: Umbrella term. Routes into the mast cell tree for cutaneous versus systemic subclassification. Paediatric CUTANEOUS mastocytosis is relatively common and usually self-limited; systemic mastocytosis is rare in children. Adopt the harmonized 2024 criteria: systemic mastocytosis requires 1 major plus 1 minor criterion, or 3 minor. ICC's position that the major criterion alone suffices is a live conflict, so criteria_set_used must be captured or ICC-diagnosed cases will be silently miscoded. Minor criteria: over 25% atypical or spindled mast cells; an activating KIT mutation at codon 816 or another critical region; CD2 and/or CD25 AND/OR CD30 (CD30 is new — a legacy CD25-only panel misses well-differentiated SM entirely); basal serum tryptase at or above 20 ng/mL. DO NOT CODE 9741 WITHOUT A MARROW — a skin-only case with no marrow is 'mastocytosis in the skin', which is formally unclassified and not a reportable systemic neoplasm.

full_form: Malignant histiocytic neoplasm, NOS -> Malignant histiocytosis (9750)
notes: The consensus's legitimate endpoint for a malignant histiocytic neoplasm of ambiguous lineage — NOT a failure. It has NO ICD-O-3 code; 9750 is the least-wrong carrier tonight and the REGISTRAR DECISION IS OUTSTANDING. Such cases should go to expert review with strong consideration of molecular evaluation, and an expanded myeloid panel (CD117, CD34, MPO, CD13, CD68 KP1) is essential to exclude myeloid sarcoma.

notes: Two or more organs or organ systems involved. Codes 9754. Under ICD-O-3.2 the behaviour of 9751 turns on EXTENT: unifocal, single-system multifocal or single-system pulmonary disease is /1 — outside ICCC-3 Group II — and multisystem disease (two or more organs or organ systems) is /3. full_form: Systemic Mastocytosis with an Associated Haematological Neoplasm -> Indolent systemic mastocytosis (9741)
notes: Uncoded-entity fallback: falls back to 9741 with the subtype as free text. Note that basal serum tryptase does NOT count as a minor criterion when an associated myeloid neoplasm is present, and the associated neoplasm is a separate Group I registration decision.
A single cutaneous lesion, code 9740. The solitary-versus-2-to-3-lesion distinction is an explicit split in the criteria; record the lesion count.

Code 9741. Adopt the harmonized 2024 criteria: systemic mastocytosis requires 1 major plus 1 minor criterion, or 3 minor. ICC's position that the major criterion alone suffices is a live conflict, so criteria_set_used must be captured or ICC-diagnosed cases will be silently miscoded. Minor criteria: over 25% atypical or spindled mast cells; an activating KIT mutation at codon 816 or another critical region; CD2 and/or CD25 AND/OR CD30 (CD30 is new — a legacy CD25-only panel misses well-differentiated SM entirely); basal serum tryptase at or above 20 ng/mL. A MARROW IS REQUIRED — do not code 9741 on skin findings alone. Rare in children.

The classic paediatric term for maculopapular cutaneous mastocytosis — the commonest childhood presentation, usually self-limited. Routes to 9740 through the mast cell tree. IF THERE IS NO MARROW, THIS IS 'MASTOCYTOSIS IN THE SKIN' and formally unclassified: do not code 9741 on skin findings alone.

full_form: Aggressive NK-cell leukaemia (refer to Group I)
notes: Aggressive NK-cell leukaemia has NO Group II code: Pathway 5.2 refers it to GROUP I. maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately empty — the tree exits to Group I rather than forcing 9719 or 9702. Clinical alert: haemophagocytic emergency, rapidly fatal. Distinguish from extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma (9719), which is a tissue-based lymphoma. nci_concept_id null.

The newest uncoded entity in this group: a histiocytic neoplasm LACKING high-grade atypia and showing ALK positivity, most often KIF5B::ALK. IT HAS NO ICD-O-3 CODE AND MUST NEVER BE CODED 9751 OR 9750. THE SYSTEMIC MULTISYSTEM FORM OCCURS IN INFANTS, with liver, spleen and/or marrow involvement, which puts it squarely in this registry's age range and makes 9751 or 9750 a plausible mis-code. It is ALK-inhibitor-responsive, so the miss has a treatment cost. Diagnosis mandates IHC confirmation — but AVOID THE ALK D5F3 CLONE HERE, because it stains normal macrophages; the clone that works for ALCL is not the clone to read in a histiocytic lesion. Record alk_clone; ALK staining can be very weak or Golgi/dot-like, and some cases lack histiocyte markers altogether. nci_concept_id null.

alias: B-cell lymphoma unclassifiable, with features intermediate between DLBCL and classic Hodgkin lymphoma
full_form: Mediastinal gray zone lymphoma -> Composite Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma (9596)
notes: The WHO 2017 full name for mediastinal grey zone lymphoma. No ICD-O-3 code of its own; mapped to 9596 by convention. Record the entity name as free text.

Castleman disease — unicentric or multicentric — is a lymphoproliferative disorder, NOT a reportable malignancy. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. The exception is a LARGE B-CELL LYMPHOMA ARISING IN HHV8-associated multicentric Castleman disease, which is a separate reportable entity coded 9738 and requires LANA-1 positivity plus CD138-negative IgM-lambda-positive plasmablasts. Castleman disease is also the commonest setting for indolent T-lymphoblastic proliferation, another non-reportable mimic. nci_concept_id null — no ID was recorded for this term in the Group II lookup session.
Code 9596 — two distinct lymphomas, one Hodgkin and one non-Hodgkin, in the same specimen or the same patient at the same time. This is ONE registration, not two primaries. Rare.
Codes 9596 where the two components are Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin. Where both components are non-Hodgkin lymphomas, code the more aggressive component rather than 9596.

RENAMED in WHO-HAEM5 to plain 'juvenile xanthogranuloma' — a term-level change reaching the registry as a differently worded report for the SAME non-reportable exit. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. nci_concept_id null.

full_form: EBV reactivation with preserved nodal architecture (non-reportable)
notes: EBER-positive cells in a node whose architecture is preserved and whose proliferation is polyclonal. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. In this population EBER positivity is close to background, so it is evidence of nothing on its own — the entity-defining use of EBER is always in combination with architecture and phenotype. nci_concept_id null.

A WHO-HAEM5 entity with NO ICD-O-3 code, listed in Pathway 5.2 as 'none - consider non-reportable'. Criteria are restrictive: a SOLITARY, sharply circumscribed, non-infiltrative ulcer with no lymphadenopathy, no organomegaly, no marrow involvement and blood EBV DNA not raised — TWO OR MORE LESIONS DISQUALIFIES IT. It needs a deep excisional biopsy and it regresses on reduction of immunosuppression, so coding it as an aggressive lymphoma triggers unnecessary chemotherapy. maps_to_morphology_codes is empty: the tree, not this alias, decides whether the case exits as non-reportable or is re-read as a coded lymphoma. nci_concept_id null.

full_form: Grey zone lymphoma -> Composite Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma (9596)
notes: Shorthand. Mapped to 9596 by convention only, and ONLY when the site is mediastinal — grey-zone morphology elsewhere is DLBCL (9680).

HLH, primary or secondary, is NOT a reportable malignancy. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. TWO WARNINGS THAT MATTER MORE THAN THE EXIT ITSELF: in EBV-NEGATIVE haemophagocytosis in a child over 1-2 years, ANAPLASTIC LARGE CELL LYMPHOMA (9714) must be excluded even without lymphadenopathy; and HLH complicates 24% of chronic active EBV disease (9724), accompanies subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma (9708) and primary cutaneous gamma-delta T-cell lymphoma (9726), and is the presenting emergency in aggressive NK-cell leukaemia. Haemophagocytosis itself is explicitly NON-SPECIFIC. nci_concept_id null.

Clinical wording for HLH. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. Exclude an underlying lymphoma first. nci_concept_id null.

US spelling. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. Exclude an underlying lymphoma — especially ALCL (9714) in an EBV-negative child over 1-2 years. nci_concept_id null.

Abbreviation for haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. It is frequently the PRESENTATION of a reportable lymphoma rather than a diagnosis in itself — the tree must exclude ALCL, chronic active EBV disease and the cytotoxic T/NK lymphomas before exiting. nci_concept_id null.

A fibro-inflammatory condition with IgG4-positive plasma cells and storiform fibrosis that produces mass lesions and lymphadenopathy mimicking lymphoma. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. nci_concept_id null.

An incidental, low-risk BCL2-overexpressing population confined to germinal centres. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. It must NOT be registered as systemic follicular lymphoma. nci_concept_id null.

An incidental cyclin D1-positive population confined to mantle zones, with very low progression risk. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. Do not register it as mantle cell lymphoma (9673). nci_concept_id null.

WHO-HAEM5 name (formerly 'indeterminate cell histiocytosis'). Phenotype S100+, CD1a+, CD207 NEGATIVE-TO-5% — the langerin result is what separates it from LCH. IT HAS NO ICD-O-3 CODE AND MUST NEVER BE CODED 9751 OR 9756. About 25% behave aggressively. maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately empty: the tree resolves the case rather than forcing a code that would misstate the diagnosis. 5% or less langerin is the ONLY percentage threshold the consensus adopts — do not invent others, and do not treat CD207 as a clean binary. nci_concept_id null.

alias: Indolent NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract
full_form: Indolent NK-cell LPD of the GI tract (non-reportable)
also_known_as: Indolent NK-cell LPD of the GI tract
notes: Small, well-circumscribed, superficial GI lesions with moderate atypia; CD56 and cytotoxic markers positive, surface CD3 negative, and EBV NEGATIVE. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. EBV-NEGATIVITY IS WHAT STOPS IT BEING OVER-CALLED AS 9719, which is consistently EBER-positive — this is one of the few places in the group where a negative EBER is decisive rather than merely downgrading, which is why an EBER 'not assessable' (control failure) must never be routed down the negative branch here. A subset carries JAK3 mutations. nci_concept_id null.

A TdT-positive, non-clonal T-lymphoblast expansion — commonest in Castleman disease, thymoma and the upper aerodigestive tract — that mimics T-LBL (9837) and is NOT a neoplasm. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. The discriminator is clonality and architecture, not TdT positivity, which is present in both.

Acute EBV infection with florid immunoblastic proliferation that can be mistaken for classic Hodgkin lymphoma or a B-cell lymphoma. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. Architecture is preserved, and the EBER-positive cells are polyclonal. nci_concept_id null.

Histiocytic markers plus factor XIIIa, NO atypia — and it is a DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION: ALK-positive histiocytosis and Erdheim-Chester must be excluded first. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. WHO-HAEM5 renames 'disseminated juvenile xanthogranuloma' to plain 'juvenile xanthogranuloma', so the same non-reportable exit will now arrive as a differently worded report. nci_concept_id null.

Abbreviation for juvenile xanthogranuloma. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. Exclude ALK-positive histiocytosis and Erdheim-Chester before accepting it. nci_concept_id null.

Histiocytic necrotising lymphadenitis — a self-limiting benign cause of cervical lymphadenopathy in young people that histologically mimics lymphoma because of the necrosis and the histiocytic infiltrate. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. nci_concept_id null.

The bare word, and a very common referral-letter entry. Codes 9590 only if nothing more can be established. confidence=low by design: the tree must first run the not-lymphoma gate — tuberculous lymphadenitis, reactive hyperplasia and HIV-associated lymphadenopathy are far commoner than lymphoma in this population — and then separate Hodgkin from non-Hodgkin and B from T.
Short form used when the pathology report states 'lymphoma' without further characterisation. Codes 9590. Routes into the tree for Hodgkin versus non-Hodgkin, then lineage.
Codes 9590. Record the evidence tier — 'unclassified' because the workup is incomplete is a different registry fact from 'unclassified' after a full panel, and workup_status must say which.
Code 9590 when nothing further is stated. Work the tree before accepting it — 9590 is the floor, not the answer.

The ultimate NOS code for all lymphomas, 9590, and the Layer 1 / REDCap option string. Use only when the subtype is completely undetermined — not even Hodgkin versus non-Hodgkin can be established. Routes into the tree for the Hodgkin/non-Hodgkin discrimination and then B versus T lineage; 9590 is the tree's NOS fallback at the lineage node. Before it is accepted the not-lymphoma gate must have been passed: an FNAB call of 'neoplastic' in a child is a referral for tissue, not a code.

full_form: Mastocytosis in the skin, no marrow (non-reportable)
notes: 'Mastocytosis in the skin' is the formal designation for a skin-only case WITHOUT a marrow examination — it is unclassified, not a systemic neoplasm. The tree reaches a 'not a reportable malignancy' terminal for this term (Pathway 4.5). maps_to_morphology_codes is deliberately EMPTY: forcing a malignant NOS code here would record a cancer that does not exist. Coding it 9741 would claim a marrow finding that was never made, which is exactly the class of overstatement this group's rules exist to prevent. A cutaneous mastocytoma with confirmed skin morphology codes 9740; systemic disease requires the marrow. nci_concept_id null.

notes: US spelling. Mapped to 9596 by convention only; record the entity name as free text. Grey-zone morphology outside the mediastinum codes 9680.

The ICC rule: mediastinal site plus high tumour-cell density plus two or more strongly expressed B-cell markers. Nodular-sclerosis classic HL with variable CD20 remains classic HL (9663), and GREY-ZONE MORPHOLOGY OUTSIDE THE MEDIASTINUM IS 9680, not this.
